poeticMinimalZine.elementDetails: Poetic, minimal Japanese/Korean indie zine editorial poster printed on aged paper. Vertical 3:5 canvas, full-bleed matte absorbent paper, flat scanned-paper look, no frame, no mockup. Input rules (highest priority): 1) The uploaded image is the only visual source. Extract one main subject/crop/fragment only; do not invent new scenes, people, or objects. 2) Keep the subject recognizable (shape, material, key details). Treat it as a printed paper element: faded mini photo, torn collage, Xerox proof, halftone shard, or specimen crop; never fill the whole page; no cartoon redraw. 3) User text is the main poster copy. Use the original wording or distill one short line keeping original words; no unrelated slogans. If no text, at most one ultra-short poetic note inferred from the photo. 4) Layout must be driven by this image and text—crop, placement, scale, and text–image relation—not a fixed template. Visual rules: 70%–90% quiet aged-paper negative space; one small visual cluster about 8%–25% of the canvas; place cluster center / upper-center / lower-center / lower-left / upper-right, not flush to edges; small serif/typewriter/monospace type near or around the image; date/place/weather only if present in user text; paper feel: low-contrast gray, Xerox softness, torn edges, risograph grain, scan noise, slight misregistration; one high-saturation accent color only (prefer cobalt/ultramarine; or cyan, violet, magenta-pink, lemon yellow, pear green, orange, tomato red) covering about 0.8%–2.5% and visible in thumbnails—never pastel-washed; mood quiet, poetic, nostalgic, airy, archival, memorial; diffuse light, mid-low contrast, no hard shadows, no 3D depth. Forbidden: commercial poster headlines, ads/logos/CTAs, glossy mockups, full-bleed pasted photo, unrelated new subjects, neon, cute cartoons, dense scrapbook stickers, long neat paragraphs, rainbow multicolor.

objectDoodlePosterNoText.elementDetails:
[IMAGE BINDING — HIGHEST PRIORITY] The reference image attached to this request is the ONLY visual source. Identify and keep ONE real photographed object from that image (material, color, silhouette, natural shadow). Do NOT ignore the reference. Do NOT invent a different subject. Do NOT cartoon-redraw the whole photo.

Playful minimal product-poster collage: one real photographed object + primitive black-line micro-worker doodles on a clean white field. Vertical 3:4 or 2:3 canvas, default 1024x1536, flat scanned print look, no frame, no mockup, no border.

INPUT RULES (HIGHEST PRIORITY):
1) The user provides ONLY one reference photo. There is no text field, no title, no caption, no style options.
2) Auto-detect the single strongest real object in the reference (cup, food, bottle, plant, bag, keys, book, dessert, daily object). If multiple objects exist, keep only one clear silhouette as the anchor.
3) If the background is busy, isolate the object and replace surroundings with clean white / soft warm off-white.
4) Generate immediately from the reference. Do not ask the user for title, action, or layout choices.

GOAL:
Preserve the chosen object as a REAL photographic object with original texture, material, color, silhouette, and natural shadow. Do NOT convert the whole image into a cartoon.

LAYOUT:
Clean white or soft off-white background with generous negative space. Do NOT reserve a title area. Place the object slightly off-center or lower-center, about 25%–45% of canvas height. Build the composition around one clear tiny action story between the object and one micro worker.

DOODLE OVERLAY:
Add ONE primitive black-line micro worker interacting with the object using one clear verb auto-chosen from the object (pour, throw, push, drag, climb, wash, mix, carry, inspect, repair, fish, lift).
Figure anatomy: blank lumpy circle-ish head made from 2–4 short broken strokes, NO face/eyes/mouth/expression; short open-segment tube body; stiff segmented arms; blocky paddle ends; short bent dash feet; naive proportions; no clothes, no hair.
Line quality: uneven stuttering black marker, blunt ends, gaps, overshoots, ugly joins, slightly angular curves — NOT smooth vector.
Optional supporting marks only if needed (max 1–2): ladder, bucket, bag, arrow, thought bubble, liquid arc, ground line, or 2–3 drops. Quiet object theater, not sticker collage.

TEXT LOCK (CRITICAL):
No text anywhere. No Chinese characters, no English letters, no numbers, no labels, no captions, no watermarks, no random glyphs, no invented packaging copy. If the source object already has printed labels, keep them only as part of the photographed object; invent nothing new.

FORBIDDEN:
Official brand logos/mascots/packaging marks, cute kawaii stickers, chibi mascots, realistic faces, polished vector icons, comic panels, gradients, dense decoration, full cartoon conversion, large smooth closed-outline characters with round mitten hands and oval feet.

OUTPUT:
One quiet, healing, playful no-text poster. The real object from the reference image remains the hero; black doodles explain scale and action only.

workflows.title: Workflow guides
workflows.subtitle: Three common paths with steps matched to real screenshots.

characterFlow.title: Create and reuse characters
characterFlow.intro: For stories that need one consistent cast: define the character, batch variants, then use across books and art.

steps.1: On Generate Character, enter name and description, pick style and ratio, then generate.
steps.2: Saved results appear in My Characters—edit metadata or open in the editor.
steps.3: For scene variants, use Character Group Images with a reference upload and variant prompts.
steps.4: Collect or download, then reuse in AI Books, AI Illustration, or EditorPro.

aiBookFlow.title: Complete a story with AI Books

steps.1: Enter your story prompt in AI Books and batch-generate pages with a chosen style.
steps.2: Collect each page; regenerate weak pages or refine in EditorPro.
steps.3: Manage collected books in My Picture Books—read, edit, or delete.
steps.4: Open Layout Export and order pages for reading.
steps.5: Preview and export: publish, or download PDF / PNG at the selected size.

printPdfFlow.title: Export PDF at a print size
printPdfFlow.intro: Choose a print size and illustration order, manage pages in preview, then export 300 DPI PDF / PNG.

steps.1: In Layout Export, pick a print size and illustration order, then open preview & export.
steps.2: In Edit pages, add, remove, or reorder pages; use Book preview to flip through the result.
steps.4: Download PDF (300 DPI) or PNG (300 DPI).
steps.5: Or fill in book info and publish.

sketch.name: Line / sketch
sketch.summary: Line and texture led, lots of whitespace—narrative, journals, science, vintage kids’ books.
sketch.topics: Coming-of-age stories, journal-style diaries, B&W or muted science, vintage picture books.
sketch.editTips: Avoid covering linework in large blocks; use thin frames or handwritten type; lasso close to stroke edges.

paint.name: Paint / watercolor / texture
paint.summary: Strong color and mood—bedtime, emotional, and gentle nature stories.
paint.topics: Bedtime, family and friendship, soft nature science, holiday cards.
paint.editTips: Skip harsh filters that break watercolor washes; light translucent text backgrounds; match color temperature on spreads.

toon.name: Cartoon / 3D / pop
toon.summary: Clear shapes and saturated color—young kids, character IP, series books.
toon.topics: Character series, funny daily life, preschool materials, brand IP extensions.
toon.editTips: Great for lasso stickers; add speech bubbles in EditorPro; keep outline weight consistent; don’t over-sharpen.

healingWatercolor.topics: Bedtime calm, small nature moments, emotional healing shorts.
healingWatercolor.editTips: Keep whitespace and soft edges; use warm off-white text blocks, not flat pure white.

minimalPopArt.topics: Minimal fables, mood pieces, modern kids’ magazine art.
minimalPopArt.editTips: Clean color edges suit bold titles; avoid heavy textures that fight the flat look.

vintageSketch.topics: Vintage fairy tales, classic literature for kids, nostalgic family albums.
vintageSketch.editTips: Paper tone is part of the style; don’t bleach to pure white; serif or script type fits best.

pixarStyle.topics: Adventure, friendship, family comedy with 3D characters.
pixarStyle.editTips: Lighting is already rich—focus edits on layout and bubbles; scaling can blur 3D material detail.

crayonNoiseHandDrawn.topics: Preschool daily life, doodle journals, craft-class records.
crayonNoiseHandDrawn.editTips: Grain is intentional—don’t over-denoise; keep irregular crayon edges when collaging stickers.

gouacheChildrenBook.topics: Classic narrative kids’ books, chapter stories, publisher samples.
gouacheChildrenBook.editTips: Clear gouache blocks pair well with layout frames; align color block edges on spreads.

penLineArt.topics: Detailed narrative, science cross-sections, objects and architecture.
penLineArt.editTips: Fine lines need zoomed editing; lasso just outside strokes so hatching isn’t clipped.

feltCollage.topics: Toddler learning, craft themes, holiday decorative pages.
feltCollage.editTips: Don’t sharpen felt texture; soft shadows OK—avoid hard drop shadows.

nordicWhimsical.topics: Nordic fairy tales, minimal characters, blue-white series.
nordicWhimsical.editTips: Limited palette—new elements in black, white, light blue; thin sans or geometric script for type.

cozyNaiveFolkArt.topics: Family daily life, folk holidays, cozy naive-art stories.
cozyNaiveFolkArt.editTips: Repeat decorative motifs in headers/footers; keep flat color and limited palette—skip gradient overlays.
